findings.problem: Greek has δεύτερον ἔτος ἤδη φεύγοντες, 'already in the second year of flight', not 'two years already'.

findings.quote: had not merely appealed to the gods and kissed the ground, as men commonly do,
findings.problem: Greek: τοὺς θεοὺς ἀσπάσαιντο (greeted/saluted the gods) and τὴν γῆν προσκυνήσαιεν (did obeisance to the earth), as other men customarily do. 'Appealed' and 'kissed the ground' are not what is said.
findings.proposed_fix: had not merely greeted the gods and bowed down to the earth, as men commonly do,

units.note: Rest of chapter checked: correlatives, the two successive battles (Romans beat Carthaginians), and names are sound.

findings.problem: Greek has ὃς ἦν μὲν οἰκεῖος Σόφακος: οἰκεῖος means a relative or kinsman, not merely a friend.

findings.quote: well suited in other respects and with a water supply close at hand.
findings.problem: The Greek breaks off mid-sentence: πρός τε τἄλλα τόπον εὐφυῆ καταλαβόμενος καὶ τὴν … (text ends at 'and the'). 'A water supply close at hand' is not in the Greek given; the English silently completes a truncated sentence.
findings.proposed_fix: well suited in other respects and ... [the Greek text breaks off here].

units.note: Also, the Greek after 'τῶν δὲ φησάντων,' has no stated content (apparent gap); English 'When they said he had' is a reasonable sense but supplies the reply. Not flagged as a fix.

findings.quote: And they did not, like tyrants, put forward even some small pretext to veil their shame
findings.problem: Greek: οὐδ᾽ οὖν, καθάπερ οἱ τύραννοι, βραχεῖαν δή τινα προβαλλόμενοι τῆς αἰσχύνης πρόφασιν: 'not even, as tyrants do, putting forward some small pretext'. Tyrants do offer a pretext; these kings did not. The English makes tyrants the contrast, inverting the sense.
findings.proposed_fix: And they did not, as even tyrants do, put forward some small pretext to veil their shame

units.note: The Greek has a supplied [ῥᾴδιον] in the sentence 'οὐ δύνανται ... ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲ βραχὺ διαπιστῆσαι'; the English sense is acceptable.
Greek breaks off at the end (μηδένα λόγον ἔτι προσίεσθαι, apparently truncated); English 'in his favor' is a slight addition but not flagged.
